edges.description: The two cell populations form the mass whose rapid, expansive growth gives the clinical picture. The tumour commonly grows infiltratively, and in one series every tumour examined had infiltrative borders and extensive permeation into the bone.

edges.description: MNTI has been reported to produce vanillylmandelic acid, which, with its heterogeneous cellular phenotype, is given as the reason for proposing a neural-crest origin. The cited sources do not describe how the tumour comes to produce it or how its production relates to the urinary level.

edges.description: In the maxilla or mandible the expansile growth presents as a rapidly growing jaw mass.
The destructive growth erodes the bone the tumour arises in, which imaging shows as a lytic lesion.
The symptoms of jaw MNTI are said to depend on the size of the swelling the growth produces, and facial asymmetry is among them.

The symptoms of jaw MNTI are said to depend on the size of the swelling the growth produces, and difficulty in feeding is among them; in one reported case the rapidly progressive swelling caused difficulty in feeding.
Epistaxis is among the symptoms that jaw MNTI is said to cause depending on the size of the swelling the growth produces. The cited source does not describe how the tumour causes the bleeding.

nodes.description: The tumour cells form two populations: large polygonal epithelioid cells that resemble melanocytes and produce melanin, which they contain in variable amounts, and smaller neuroblast-like round cells. The tumour's origin is attributed to the neural crest, but that origin is also described as putative and the histogenesis of MNTI as still unresolved.

evidence.snippet: The origin of the tumor is the neural crest. ... Microscopically, large polygonal epithelioid cells resembling melanocytes, with variable deposits of melanin, and smaller neuroblast-like round cells characterize MNTI.

evidence.reference_title: Melanotic Neuroectodermal Tumor of Infancy (MNTI) and Pineal Anlage Tumor (PAT) Harbor A Medulloblastoma Signature by DNA Methylation Profiling.
evidence.snippet: MNTI is a rare neoplasm of putative neural crest origin, preferentially arising in craniofacial sites. The histogenesis of MNTI remains elusive, with divergent theories (odontogenic, primordial germ cell, and a neural crest origin) being hypothesized over the years, leading to inconsistent—and confusing—nomenclature in the literature
Histologically, it is composed of a biphasic population of cells, consisting of epithelioid melanin-producing cells and primitive neurogenic cells in a fibrocollagenous stroma.

evidence.snippet: The large polygonal epithelioid cells were melanin-producing and showed vesicular nuclei, prominent nucleoli and eosinophilic cytoplasm.

nodes.description: A review of jaw MNTI states that, because of the tumour's melanin content, the lesion appears clinically as a bluish-black swelling, usually covered by the oral mucosa, and regards a maxillary swelling with a bluish-black hue and a rapid course in an infant as a pathognomonic clinical sign of oral MNTI. In the case the authors present, the swelling looked like a coin-sized, marble-like elevation with blanching of the overlying mucosa and a central melanaceous hue, and that hue, with the patient's age and the site, was the basis for the provisional diagnosis.

evidence.reference_title: Melanotic Neuroectodermal Tumor of Infancy of Jaws: A Case Report and Review of Literature.
evidence.snippet: Due to the melanin content of the tumor, clinically, the lesion will appear as a bluish-black swelling usually draped by the oral mucosa. Maxillary swelling with a bluish-black hue and a rapid course in an infant can be considered as a clinical pathognomic sign to diagnose an oral MNTI.

nodes.description: Urinary vanillylmandelic acid (VMA) is raised in some patients. In a review pooling 250 jaw MNTI cases, including the authors' own, urine VMA was elevated in 22 and normal in 31, and 197 cases had no VMA information. Raised VMA can point to a neuroectodermal tumour, but a normal level does not rule MNTI out.

evidence.reference_title: Melanotic Neuroectodermal Tumor of Infancy of Jaws: A Case Report and Review of Literature.
evidence.snippet: After removing the duplicate articles and articles not following the inclusion criteria, full-text screening of the remaining articles was conducted to record the parameters such as age, sex, location, management option, recurrence, and urine VMA levels. ... A total of 178 articles discussing 249 cases of MNTI in the jawbone were selected for data extraction. ... The final number of cases included in this review was 250 including the current case we described. ... Data on vanillylmandelic acid (VMA) levels in the patient population revealed that 31 (12.4%) cases exhibited normal levels, while 22 (8.8%) cases indicated elevated VMA levels. In 197 (78.8%) cases, lacked information regarding VMA levels. ... Raised VMA levels can indicate a neuroectodermal tumor, but its absence does not rule out the disease.

nodes.description: MNTI most commonly affects the maxilla of infants in the first year of life and may also arise in the mandible, skull, brain, epididymis and other rare sites. Its expansive, destructive and rapid growth and its effects on surrounding tissues are its most obvious clinical features.

nodes.description: The tumour may present as a rapidly expanding, lobulated, non-ulcerated and painless mass, most often of the maxilla. In a 472-case systematic review, which Xia et al. (2021) describe as the largest, 62.2% of tumours involved the maxilla, 15.6% the skull and 7.8% the mandible.

nodes.description: Surgery is the mainstay of treatment; a 2026 expert consensus gives cure rates of 80%-90%, and its abstract does not say which case series the figure comes from or how cure was defined. Complete surgical resection is regarded as the gold standard, and incomplete resection has been proposed as one of the main reasons for frequent recurrences.
